title: Keld Keep and the First Seam
caption: The Warden's fortress city against the Rim and the deep survey cut into the stone beneath it, drawn cold and mineral as the Keep's own survey-clerks would draw it: the walled Keep with the Warden's hall and the mine-reeve's room; the Rim Road coming up from Sill and going on ten leagues to the Cold Pass and its survey post; the Listening Stones five leagues higher in the Rim; and below, the timbered shaft of the First Seam with its galleries, the Descent, the Duelling Floor cut into the stone with nine clamps to the floor and the tenth behind the board, the survey room holding the crossed-out entry of Y.H. 588 and its branching red mark, the Ninth Gallery with the tin lined with warm-stone, a seam-serpent's passing entered only as a change in the numbers, and the hot-lead warning of the Sweating. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with a compass, a league scale, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the measure before the name, the Warden's claim, the once-a-year reading of the paper, and the insistence that no map is honest past the last pass.
